About Skinkpedia

Skinkpedia is an independent educational website focused on skinks: the lizard family Scincidae. The site helps readers understand skink biology, identify wild species, compare commonly kept pet skinks, and make more informed husbandry decisions.

What Skinkpedia covers

Skinkpedia is organized around several connected subject areas:

  • skink taxonomy, anatomy and natural history;
  • wild-skink identification and regional distribution;
  • pet-skink species selection;
  • enclosure, diet, lighting, heating and humidity;
  • handling, enrichment and general health monitoring;
  • backyard coexistence and humane exclusion;
  • species-specific guides for blue-tongue, crocodile and other skinks.

The site separates broad family-level guidance from species-specific husbandry because values such as temperature, humidity, enclosure size and diet should not be transferred from one species to another without evidence.

How our articles are developed

Articles are built from a structured topical map so that each URL has a defined subject and does not unnecessarily duplicate nearby pages.

During research and editing, Skinkpedia prioritizes:

  1. peer-reviewed research;
  2. veterinary guidance;
  3. universities and academic institutions;
  4. zoos and government wildlife agencies;
  5. recognized conservation organizations;
  6. specialist husbandry references;
  7. commercial product specifications only when the product itself is being discussed.

Exact numerical care recommendations are kept at the species level wherever possible.

See our Sources & Research Methodology for more detail.

Who writes Skinkpedia?

Skinkpedia is researched and published by Farrukh Abdullah.

The author role is editorial and research-focused. Skinkpedia does not present the author as a veterinarian, zoologist or licensed wildlife professional unless an article explicitly identifies a qualified contributor and their role.

See the Farrukh Abdullah author page.

What Skinkpedia is not

Skinkpedia is not a veterinary clinic and does not diagnose or treat animals.

Health articles are designed to help readers:

  • recognize husbandry-related risk factors;
  • notice warning signs;
  • understand when home observation is reasonable;
  • know when a reptile veterinarian or wildlife professional should be contacted.

Corrections and updates

Taxonomy, conservation status, regulations, product availability and husbandry recommendations can change.

If we discover a substantive factual error, we correct the article and, where useful, explain the correction. See our Corrections Policy.

Commercial relationships

Some care and equipment pages may contain affiliate links. If Skinkpedia earns a commission from a qualifying purchase, that relationship should be disclosed clearly and should not change the editorial standard applied to the recommendation.

See the Affiliate Disclosure.
